Устаревшее значение

Вы узнаете

Когда оптимизатор может разделить повторяющееся выражение и когда общее значение успело устареть.

Устранение общих подвыражений заменяет повторяющееся выражение временной переменной. Это допустимо, только если ничто из читаемого выражением не записывалось между повторами. Оптимизатор однажды вычислял временную переменную в начале тела, что бы ни происходило дальше: она читала локальную переменную выше её объявления, и код не компилировался, или значение до переприсваивания, и код компилировался, но был неверен. stale_operand(5) равно 106, а дефектный компилятор возвращал 12. shared_product(3, 4) равно 24: пока между двумя произведениями ничего не записано, разделение по-прежнему верно. Правило теперь живёт в отдельной спеке cse_hoist.t27.

Попробовать

Запустите stale_operand(5), затем folded_twice(131071) и прочитайте правило под каждым. Потом попробуйте shared_product при y, равном 0.

Common subexpression elimination shares a repeated expression, and may only do it when nothing changed in between. Four small functions pin the rule. Pick one, set its input and read the result.

specs/compiler/codegen_conformance.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/codegen_conformance.t27 -- the reference path (`t27c gen` + `zig test`) computes what the
; spec says. One case per silent miscompile: each test fails on the code the defective compiler generated
; and passes once the defect is fixed. Add the next case here; do not open a spec per bug (#8963).
; --
; #6549: the parser keeps no parentheses, and gen-zig wrote a unary operator straight in front of its
; operand. `-(a + b)` ran as `-a + b`, `!(a and b)` as `!a and b`, `~(a | b)` as `~a | b`. Typecheck
; stayed green; specs/ml/loss/binary_crossentropy_loss.t27 returned the loss with the wrong sign.
; --
; #8197, #7703, #2629: common_subexpr_elim replaced a repeated expression by a temp computed at the top of
; the body, whatever happened in between. The temp read a local above its declaration (a compile error), or
; a value from before a reassignment: stale_operand(5) compiled and returned 12. The rule now lives in
; specs/compiler/cse_hoist.t27.
; --
; #8971, gen-rust: a char literal became a Rust `char` (not a u8), a read-only `[]usize` parameter a
; `Vec<usize>` (a caller passing a slice failed), and a `[]const u8` parameter `&'static str` unless the file
; sliced somewhere. The Zig tests below pass either way; the cases are the Rust that `t27c gen-rust` writes
; for them, which rustc rejected and now compiles.
; --
; #8891, gen-rust: constructs that pass test-report but gave Rust that rustc refused. `return E.x` from a `?E`
; fn was not wrapped in Some; a bare `.x` compared with an enum stayed unqualified; `[N][]const u8` became
; `Vec<const u8>`; an anonymous struct return type reached rustc verbatim; a `[]u8` slice returned where the
; signature says Vec; a usize stored into a u64 field was not cast; a parameter named `self` was kept. `@log2`
; (emitted verbatim) is checked in bootstrap/tests/backend_behaviour.rs, because t27b has no f64 log2 and this
; file is in its corpus. Payload enum variants (`Gap(u32)`) are not here: Zig blocks them too (#9134).
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module CodegenConformance;

fn negated_sum(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    return -(a + b);
}

fn negated_float_sum(t: f64, p: f64) -> f64 {
    return -(t * p + (1.0 - t) * p);
}

fn nand(a: bool, b: bool) -> bool {
    return !(a and b);
}

fn nor_bits(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
    return ~(a | b);
}

test unary_minus_negates_the_whole_sum {
    assert negated_sum(1, 2) == -3;
    assert negated_sum(0, 2) == -2;
    assert negated_float_sum(0.0, 0.5) == -0.5;
}

test logical_not_negates_the_whole_conjunction {
    assert nand(true, false);
    assert nand(false, false);
    assert !nand(true, true);
}

test bitwise_not_inverts_the_whole_disjunction {
    assert nor_bits(1, 2) == 252;
    assert nor_bits(0, 0) == 255;
}

fn stale_operand(x: u32) -> u32 {
    var p : u32 = x + 1;
    x = 99;
    var q : u32 = x + 1;
    return p + q;
}

fn counted_three_times() -> u32 {
    var count : u32 = 0;
    count = count + 1;
    count = count + 1;
    count = count + 1;
    return count;
}

fn folded_twice(x: u32) -> u32 {
    var s : u32 = x;
    s = (s & 65535) + (s >> 16);
    s = (s & 65535) + (s >> 16);
    return s;
}

fn shared_product(x: u32, y: u32) -> u32 {
    var p : u32 = x * y;
    var q : u32 = x * y;
    return p + q;
}

test a_repeat_after_a_reassignment_reads_the_new_value {
    assert stale_operand(5) == 106;
}

test a_counter_bumped_three_times_counts_three {
    assert counted_three_times() == 3;
}

test a_fold_applied_twice_carries_twice {
    // 131071 = 0x1FFFF folds to 65536, and 65536 folds to 1
    assert folded_twice(131071) == 1;
}

test an_untouched_repeat_still_shares_its_value {
    assert shared_product(3, 4) == 24;
}

fn count_byte(text: []const u8, c: u8) -> usize {
    var n : usize = 0;
    var i : usize = 0;
    while (i < text.len) {
        if (text[i] == c) {
            n += 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    return n;
}

fn is_digit(c: u8) -> bool {
    return c >= '0' and c <= '9';
}

fn first_plus(xs: []usize, k: usize) -> usize {
    return xs[0] + xs[k];
}

fn first_plus_of_three(k: usize) -> usize {
    var xs : [3]usize = [4, 5, 6];
    return first_plus(&xs, k);
}

test a_char_literal_is_a_byte {
    assert is_digit('7');
    assert !is_digit('x');
}

test a_byte_slice_parameter_reads_bytes {
    assert count_byte("banana", 'a') == 3;
    assert count_byte("", 'a') == 0;
}

test a_read_only_slice_parameter_takes_a_slice {
    assert first_plus_of_three(2) == 10;
    assert first_plus_of_three(1) == 9;
}

enum Size { small, big }

fn size_of(x: u32) -> ?Size {
    if (x > 10) {
        return Size.big;
    }
    return null;
}

fn size_name(s: Size) -> []const u8 {
    if (s == .big) {
        return "big";
    }
    return "small";
}

const NAMES : [3][]const u8 = ["a", "bb", "ccc"];

fn name_len(i: usize) -> usize {
    return NAMES[i].len;
}

fn verdict(x: u32) -> struct { ok: bool, code: u32 } {
    if (x > 10) {
        return .{ .ok = false, .code = 1 };
    }
    return .{ .ok = true, .code = 0 };
}

fn head(xs: []u8, n: usize) -> []u8 {
    return xs[0..n];
}

struct Tally {
    n: u64,
}

fn tally(xs: []u8) -> Tally {
    return Tally { n: xs.len, };
}

fn tally_bump(self: *Tally, by: u64) -> u64 {
    self.n = self.n + by;
    return self.n;
}

test an_enum_literal_returned_as_an_optional_is_some {
    assert size_of(1) == null;
    assert size_of(11).? == Size.big;
}

test a_bare_enum_literal_compares_with_an_enum {
    assert size_name(.big).len == 3;
    assert size_name(.small).len == 5;
}

test a_table_of_strings_keeps_each_length {
    assert name_len(0) == 1;
    assert name_len(2) == 3;
}

test an_anonymous_struct_return_carries_its_fields {
    const r = verdict(11);
    assert r.ok == false;
    assert r.code == 1;
    assert verdict(3).ok;
}

test a_returned_slice_keeps_its_bytes {
    var a : [3]u8 = [3]u8{9, 8, 7};
    const h = head(&a, 2);
    assert h.len == 2;
    assert h[1] == 8;
}

test a_length_stored_in_a_u64_field_and_a_self_parameter {
    var a : [3]u8 = [3]u8{1, 2, 3};
    var t : Tally = tally(&a);
    assert t.n == 3;
    assert tally_bump(&t, 2) == 5;
}
